_📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Use `const` for `routeSegment`.**

`routeSegment` is not reassigned. ESLint reports `prefer-const` on Line 25.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-      let routeSegment = item.name.replace(/\[(.*?)\]/g, '{$1}');
+      const routeSegment = item.name.replace(/\[(.*?)\]/g, '{$1}');
```
</details>

**Replace the placeholder with executable route-group tests.**

This suite has no test case or assertion. The CI suite can pass while `getImplementedOperations` incorrectly includes a route-group name in the API path.

Import `getImplementedOperations` and create a temporary route tree. Assert that `(auth)/users/route.ts` produces `/api/users`. Add a nested dynamic-segment case and clean up the temporary directory after each test.

As per path instructions, review `**/*.test.ts` files for assertion quality and edge cases rather than stylistic formatting.

**Add an executable regression test for route groups.**

The new branch changes the API path contract. A directory such as `(auth)` must not appear in `baseRoute`, while normal and dynamic directories must still append their segments. `tests/scripts/check-api-contract.test.ts` currently contains only a placeholder for this behavior. Add a test with a route such as `(auth)/users/[id]/route.ts` and assert `/api/users/{id}`.
